examples.japanese: {世界的|せかいてき}に{有名|ゆうめい}な{画家|がか}だ。
この{問題|もんだい}は{世界的|せかいてき}な{規模|きぼ}で{取|と}り{組|く}む{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: This problem needs to be addressed on a global scale.

examples.japanese: {世界的|せかいてき}な{不況|ふきょう}の{影響|えいきょう}で、{多|おお}くの{企業|きぎょう}が{経営|けいえい}{難|なん}に{陥|おちい}った。
examples.english: Due to the global recession, many companies fell into financial difficulty.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{世界的|せかいてき}に{活躍|かつやく}するバイオリニストだ。
examples.english: She is a violinist active on the world stage.

notes:
Used as a na-adjective or adverb (with に) to describe something that has worldwide scope, significance, or recognition. Often implies prestige when describing people or their achievements (world-class, internationally renowned).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {世界的|せかいてき}に{有名|ゆうめい}: world-famous
- {世界的|せかいてき}な{規模|きぼ}: global scale
- {世界的|せかいてき}な{傾向|けいこう}: worldwide trend
- {世界的|せかいてき}な{企業|きぎょう}: global company
- {世界的|せかいてき}に{活躍|かつやく}する: be active on the world stage

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {国際的|こくさいてき}: international — emphasizes relations or cooperation between nations, while {世界的|せかいてき} focuses on worldwide scope
- グローバル: global — a loanword used especially in business contexts (グローバル{企業|きぎょう}, グローバル{化|か})
- {全世界|ぜんせかい}: the entire world — used as a noun, not as an adjective modifier
